spec: Read lines from standard input. Each non-blank line contains one integer, possibly negative and possibly surrounded by spaces. Print the sum of all the integers on one line. If a non-blank line is not a valid integer, print `invalid line N` (N is the 1-based line number) to standard error and exit with status 1 without printing anything to standard output.

Read all of standard input and split it into words on whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines). Lowercase each word (the input is ASCII). Print the 3 most frequent words, one per line, as `COUNT WORD`, sorted by count descending; break ties by which word first appeared earlier in the input. If there are fewer than 3 distinct words, print all of them. Print nothing for empty input.

tests.stdin: the cat the dog The end cat
b a b c a b d

spec: For each line of standard input, print `ok` if the brackets ( ) [ ] { } in that line are balanced and correctly nested, otherwise print `bad`. Ignore every other character. An empty line is `ok`.

For each line of standard input, print its run-length encoding: every maximal run of one repeated character is written as that character followed by the run length, so `aaabccdd` becomes `a3b1c2d2`. An empty line prints an empty line. The input is ASCII.

Standard input is CSV whose first line is the header `name,qty,price`, followed by rows such as `apple,3,25`. qty and price are non-negative integers; there are no quotes or spaces. Blank lines are ignored. For each distinct name, in order of first appearance, print `NAME TOTAL` where TOTAL is the sum of qty*price over that name's rows. Then print `TOTAL GRAND` where GRAND is the sum over all rows.

The program receives one command-line argument N with 0 <= N <= 2000000. Print the number of primes less than or equal to N on the first line, and the largest such prime on the second line, or `none` if there is no such prime.

Print the lines of standard input in reverse order. Within each printed line, reverse the order of its whitespace-separated words and join them with single spaces. A line with no words prints as an empty line.

tests.stdin:
one two three
  hello   world 

last
tests.stdout:
last

world hello
three two one

spec: Print each distinct line of standard input once, in order of first appearance; lines are compared exactly after removing a trailing carriage return. Then print `removed N`, where N is the number of duplicate lines that were skipped.

tests.stdin:
a
b
a
c
b
a
